<translation>
<pb n="178"/>On a cloth from a cemetery or similar material, one should draw an image of either a man or a woman using substances of the elements <note>referring to ritual paints or minerals</note>. One should then imagine that from the complete transformation of the syllable **Hūṃ**, a sharp axe appears in one's own hand. With that, while reciting the syllable **Phaṭ**, one cuts the neck of the object to be accomplished <note>the enemy</note>. At that time, it is said that "the neck of the enemy will be cut." For that very reason, it is stated: "knowing them to be the object to be accomplished," referring to kings and others. The phrase "possessing the nature of an exceptional body, speech, and mind" refers to those endowed with a very beautiful body. "The superior, middle, and inferior" refers to the Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, and Shudras <note>the four traditional Indian castes</note>. To those, one does not provide benefit because of their unrighteousness. For that very reason, "remaining in great heedlessness" refers to performing wrathful activities. By this application—the application of the axe—it is certain that "they will be reduced to the fifth state" <note>a euphemism for death</note>. Regarding the phrase "the union of the nectar hearth" and so forth, during a time of heavy rain, one who dwells in the meditative absorption of **Amṛtakuṇḍalin** <gloss>The Swirling Nectar</gloss> should imagine a yellow crossed-vajra <term>viśvavajra</term> arisen from the syllable **Hūṃ** in the direction of the sky over a village or city. In its center, one imagines a blazing vajra arisen from the syllable **Hūṃ**. If one meditates that the rain is dried up by the masses of flames arising from that, it is shown that "the rain will be halted." The phrase "the great mandala of the Vajra Realm" <term>Vajradhātu-mahāmaṇḍala</term> and so forth refers to the time of drawing the great mandala when wind, rain, lightning, and so forth arise from the sky, or when water, snakes, and so forth emerge from beneath the mandala. The word "and so forth" includes earthquakes and the appearance of flesh-eating demons <term>piśāca</term>. "Applied by others" refers to obstacles created by non-Buddhists such as **Gaṇapati** and others. Whenever these occur, at that time, from the complete transformation of the Lord **Amitābha**, one imagines oneself as the noble **Hayagrīva**, with three faces, six arms, and three eyes, standing in the posture with the left leg extended <pb n="179"/> towards the enemies. If one imagines that the masses of flames arising from his hand-symbols burn and reduce to ashes the host of obstacles dwelling in the ten directions, it is shown that at that time "the wind and so forth will be pacified." The phrase "if such a nature is not realized" and so forth indicates that without such meditation, the activity of the Yogini, which consists of drawing the mandala, will not be accomplished. Here too, in wrathful activities, the "killing of the seed" by the syllable **Phaṭ**, which kills the obstacles of both one's own school and other schools, should be applied at the time when enemies cause harm. Now, concerning the phrase "now" and so forth: a yogi who practices with elaboration dwells in a three-storied divine palace. Having directed the mind toward the Wisdom Body <term>jñānakāya</term> of whichever deity one identifies with—such as **Vairocana** through self-consecration—and having placed the four seals <term>mudrā</term> of the commitment <term>samaya</term>, who are beautiful in form and very well adorned, in the four directions, one then enjoys the five sensory qualities together with them. It is shown that by the stages of meditative union, withdrawal <term>pratyāhāra</term>, and meditative concentration <term>dhyāna</term>, one will experience Great Bliss <term>mahāsukha</term>. "Generated through the stage of wisdom" refers to the elaboration through the stage of self-consecration. The phrase "that application" is a brief presentation. "Visualizing in an instant" is the detailed explanation. By that, the stages such as "obtaining the proximity of appearance" are refuted. "In the center of the four seats" means in the center of the seats of the four goddesses. The phrase "the body of the Great Vajradhara" is merely an illustration; one should also meditate on the bodies of **Vairocana** and the others. "By knowing the reality of the deity" means knowing the four goddesses together with oneself as the essence of the five wisdoms. "In the places of **Locanā** and the others" refers to the East and other directions. Through that stage of total purity, the obsession with external objects is abandoned, and acting like an ordinary person is also refuted <pb n="180"/> as well. "Correctly learning the mantras and seals" means that the seal in which the mantra is primary is the "Mantra Seal," which is the Great Vehicle of Secret Mantra. Learning it correctly means reaching the end of the stages of hearing and so forth and demonstrating it to others. "The thorough investigation of the entities of **Locanā** and the others" means meditating on them in the form of the four Mothers of the families. The "four women" are exactly four. "Day and night" means always. The phrase "with all ornaments" and so forth shows that they are adorned with innate qualities and the attributes of their attire. "The lotus of one's own heart" refers to one's own mind. The "lotus of the mouth" is the lotus of the face. "Expanded" means that after generating joy in that way, one should think: "whatever is the nature of the five chakras <note>energy centers</note> is mind-only, and nothing else." Through the phrase "the five rays of light" and so forth, it is shown that "one should experience that Great Bliss together with the stage of withdrawal <term>pratyāhāra</term>, characterized by the proximity of the senses and their objects." The phrase "acting in that way" and so forth shows that "one will become equal to the five Tathagatas such as **Vairocana**." "Acting together with even a single seal" refers to a yogi who possesses the practice without elaboration. The intention is that a yogi of Great **Vajradhara** and so forth takes a seal <note>consort</note> from any class, such as a Brahmin, and generates oneself and her in the forms of **Vairocana**, **Locanā**, and so forth. Then, traveling from place to place, eating whatever food is found, and dwelling in places solitary from people such as forests, one trains in the luminosity that is the essence of the purity of the three wisdoms. It is shown that "at 그 time one will become like the Great **Vajradhara**." "Having completely abandoned the ordinary nature" refers to the Mantra Body accomplished through the stage of wisdom. "After that" means from that cause. "The Lord" refers to...
</translation>

<summary>This text describes advanced tantric rituals including wrathful liberation rites using a symbolic axe, the pacification of elemental disturbances like rain and wind through deity yoga, and the practice of Great Bliss through the union of the practitioner and consort-seals visualized as Buddhas and their consorts.</summary>
<keywords>Yamantaka, wrathful activity, Hayagriva, Vajradhatu Mandala, Mahasuka, five wisdoms, four goddesses, consort practice, luminosity, Vajradhara</keywords>
